newsitem.title: SYRIA: Assad says Syria wants to resume peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Assad says Syria wants to resume peace talks.

text.p: President Hafez al-Assad told France's foreign minister on Thursday that Syria wanted to break the impasse in peace talks with Israel but the Israeli government was blocking the resumption of negotiations.
Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara, who attended the meeting between Assad and French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette, told reporters that Damascus was still hopeful for peace with Israel.
Speaking to reporters at Damascus airport while seeing off de Charette, Shara said:
"President Assad told Mr. de Charette that Syria has a desire to break the deadlock and the dilemma of the peace process but Israel was blocking the resumption of the peace talks.
"The situation in the region is very tense and might explode. Syria does not want that and it is still hopeful that a just and comprehensive peace might be achieved in the region," Shara said.
De Charette also expressed deep concern about the stalemate in the peace negotiations between Syria and Israel and said Paris would continue to work with all parties to find a solution.
He said the gap was still very wide between positions of Syria and Israel.

Syria wants to resume talks with Israel, which broke off a year ago, from the point where they left off with the previous Israeli government while current Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu wants to restart the talks without conditions.

Syria says that Israel's labour-led government, which was defeated by Netanyahu, had agreed during sporadic talks launched in 1991 to withdraw fully from the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967.

"The gap between Syria and Israel is very wide," de Charette said. "We understand the Syrian position...(but) all those who care about the peace process and the resumption of talks should devote their efforts for peace."
The French minister, who came from Israel on Wednesday, left for lebanon, the last leg of his tour which is aimed at reviving the peace talks between Israel and its two Arab neighbours.

"The situation of the peace process is a cause of big concern. I expressed France's deep anxiety about the stalemate and the dangers which might result because of the suspension of the negotiations," he said.

French foreign ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux told Reuters France expressed big concern during talks in Damascus and Israel about the increase in tension between Israel and Lebanon's pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas in south Lebanon.
He said that France feared that the continuation of the stalemate might lead to resumption of violence in the region.
France is current head of a five-nation group set up last year to monitor a ceasefire between Israel and Hizbollah guerrillas who are fighting Israeli presence in south lebanon.
The other members are the United States, Israel, Lebanon and Syria, who has 35,000 troops in Lebanon.

"We are worried and concerned about the resumption of tension in south Lebanon. We believe there is a big need for resumption of the peace negotiations because the monitoring group could not be an alternative to real peace," Doutriaux said.
